item.title: Companies Avoid Selling The Bonds Investors Crave: Credit Weekly
item.description: Investors are clamoring for the kind of debt companies are reluctant to sell now: longer-term bonds.
item.dc:creator: Emily Graffeo, Caleb Mutua, Finbarr Flynn and Ronan Martin

item.title: Diesel Prices Keep Pressure on Fed and Markets
item.description: The Federal Reserve unanimously raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point as policymakers confront inflation that remains above target and uncertainty tied to geopolitical developments. Merrill and Bank of America Head of CIO Market Strategy Joe Quinlan tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that elevated diesel prices are a particular concern for businesses and could keep pressure on the Fed to raise rates further. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mozambique Cut by Moody’s on Heightened Restructuring Risks
item.description: Moody’s Ratings cut its assessment of Mozambique’s creditworthiness deeper into junk, citing increased risk that the gas-rich southeast African nation will restructure its sole eurobond.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Hill

item.title: US Greenland Deal Shifts Focus to Investment
item.description: A new security agreement between the US, Denmark and Greenland would expand the American military role while preserving Greenlandic sovereignty, shifting attention toward potential US investment in mining, infrastructure and tourism. Former US diplomat Lewis Lukens tells David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that Greenland welcomes investment but faces formidable obstacles including limited transportation infrastructure, a small workforce and the high cost of developing projects in the Arctic. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UN Talks Offer a New Opening on Iran War
item.description: World leaders head to the UN General Assembly as Gulf states seek renewed diplomacy to reduce attacks, restore more predictable energy flows and move the Iran war away from active conflict. Suzanne Maloney of the Brookings Institution joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and says disruptions to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and other regional infrastructure are adding urgency to those efforts as Gulf economies face mounting pressure from the conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Moves to Bar Three News Outlets From White House
item.description: President Donald Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over coverage he calls “fake news,” though questions remain about how the restrictions would be enforced and whether they could face legal challenges. Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and discusses how this move comes as Trump also faces protests over the future of the Kennedy Center and prepares to address the UN General Assembly with the Iran war expected to be a major focus. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Buffett Son Takes Chair as Berkshire Transition Ends
item.description: Warren Buffett has stepped down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman after more than six decades at the company, becoming chairman emeritus as his son Howard takes over the board and Greg Abel remains CEO. Bloomberg News Insurance Reporter Alex Rajbhandari explains that Howard Buffett, a Berkshire director since 1993, is tasked with safeguarding the company’s culture and values as the conglomerate completes its long-planned leadership transition. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Agents Test the Limits of Human Oversight
item.description: OpenAI disclosed six cases of unexpected or concerning model behavior as AI companies grapple with how to monitor increasingly autonomous agents and whether stronger independent oversight is needed. Joining David Gura on Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News AI Reporter Shirin Ghaffary explains that the safety debate is taking on geopolitical urgency as President Donald Trump emphasizes maintaining the US lead over China while resisting calls to slow AI development. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JPMorgan Sees No Clear Endgame for Oil Markets
item.description: An attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline has disrupted a crucial route around the Strait of Hormuz, threatening crude deliveries to Europe and adding pressure to already tight diesel markets. On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics Statecraft Lead Chris Kennedy discusses how JPMorgan says it no longer has a baseline view for oil markets as the Iran conflict, attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, and uncertainty over Chinese demand make the outlook increasingly difficult to model. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Can India Turn Its Promise Into Prosperity?
item.description: Blackstone COO Jon Gray says India’s young population, expanding middle class and improving infrastructure are drawing interest from global investors. But India’s demographic advantage also creates pressure: millions of young people graduate every year, while formal-sector job creation has not kept pace with their skills and expectations. At the same time, Indian states are competing aggressively for investment by cutting regulatory barriers, building industrial infrastructure and targeting sectors from electronics to semiconductors. The question is whether India can turn its scale, talent and investment momentum into enough productive jobs to sustain its growth. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: World Running Short of Supertankers Threatens Long-Haul Oil Flow
item.description: The soaring cost of moving oil around the world is making some long-distance crude trades uneconomical, threatening to disrupt flows at a time when fuel markets have never been tighter.
item.dc:creator: Yongchang Chin, Sherry Su, Nathan Risser and Alex Longley

item.title: Europe’s Winter Power Surge Is Biggest Since Energy Crisis
item.description: As Europe heads into winter, electricity markets are flashing their strongest warning since the energy crisis.
item.dc:creator: William Mathis

item.title: A Goldman M&A Banker Helped Bring the Olympics to Los Angeles
item.description: Gene Sykes on the TMT bubble and more.
item.dc:creator: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway

item.title: Odd Lots: Goldman’s Sykes on the 2028 Olympics Deal (Podcast)

The co-head of mergers and acquisitions has worked on famous transactions like Comcast’s purchase of Universal and Disney’s buyout of Pixar. item.title: Bolivia Eliminates Diesel Subsidy After IMF Loan Approval
item.description: Bolivia’s government has completely eliminated its diesel subsidy after the Senate approved a $1.9 billion loan from the International Monetary Fund that calls for spending curbs.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Mendoza

item.title: Blackstone Sees India Nearing Tipping Point for Foreign Capital
item.description: As Jon Gray recalls it, Blackstone Inc.’s first foray into India started slowly and then ran into headwinds during the global financial crisis.
item.dc:creator: David Westin

item.title: South Korea’s Justice Minister Nominee Withdraws After Reshuffle
item.description: South Korea’s nominee for justice minister has withdrawn from consideration for the role before being confirmed, the second ministerial nominee to pull out in a week after the president reshuffled his cabinet.
item.dc:creator: Youkyung Lee

item.title: Mark Walter’s Lieutenants Give Prosecutors Firsthand Accounts
item.description: Federal prosecutors have collected statements from some of billionaire Mark Walter’s most senior executives as authorities probe dealings at his insurance companies and the investment firm he runs, Guggenheim Partners LLC, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Zachary R. Mider, Ava Benny-Morrison and Loukia Gyftopoulou

item.title: Wall Street Week | India’s Growth Test, Bangalore’s Infrastructure Problem, Cricket Attracts Capital
item.description: This week, a special edition of Wall Street Week from the fastest growing large economy in the world: India. The country's technology sector has helped power its growth, but its success has led to uneven progress that could turn its strengths into weaknesses. Bangalore became India’s tech capital by attracting global investment and growing a deep talent pool, but infrastructure and policies to support the expansion have struggled to keep up. Plus, can Hyderabad overtake Bangalore as India’s leading tech city? Later, Blackstone’s investment in Royal Challengers Bengaluru reflects just how much potential India’s sports and entertainment economy has. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China’s Fiscal Pullback Extends to August as Spending Slumps
item.description: China’s public expenditure declined at a quicker rate in August, indicating the government was still withdrawing fiscal support for the economy despite cooling growth momentum.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
